subject: Medigen: request for tenant-scoped log deletion evidence and exception handling
messages:
From: Marco Salazar <marco.salazar@medigen.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medigen.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tenant-scoped deletion evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Ava,

We're preparing for a customer audit next month and need to provide evidence that tenant-scoped ephemeral/session logs for our account are deleted in accordance with the 30-day TTL described in the SIG. Specifically, the auditor will want:

- A short description of the deletion process (how deletions are triggered and verified)
- A sample of deletion logs showing object identifiers and timestamps (redacted if necessary)
- Any policy artifacts (lifecycle rules, retention config) and a short attestation that the policy was applied to our tenant only

Also: if there are any documented customer-specific exceptions (temporary hold, legal hold, extended retention), please surface the approval channel and any compensating controls we would expect.

Can you confirm what you can share (and any redaction rules)? If possible, we'd like to receive artifacts by 2027-06-14 so we can include them in the binder.

Thanks,
Marco
Security Operations
Medigen Therapeutics
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Marco Salazar <marco.salazar@medigen.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped deletion evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Marco — thanks for the clear list. I pulled the scope you requested into the team and we can provide the following artifacts and notes: 

1) Retention policy document (attached): retention-policy-2027.pdf — describes default TTLs for ephemeral/session logs (30 days) and the distinction between tenant-scoped objects and aggregated telemetry.

2) Deletion evidence sample (attached): sample-deletion-log-20270610.csv — this is a redacted export showing object id hashes, deletion timestamp (ISO), and tenant id prefix. We will mask any PII but preserve timestamps and object lifecycle states for the auditor.

3) Audit trail & verifiable manifests: we can provide an S3 lifecycle manifest and the object-versioning manifest for the retention window upon request — these contain object keys and version IDs; we'll redact payloads.

4) Implementation notes: ephemeral sessions are stored in a tenant-scoped bucket (with per-tenant prefixes) and removed by an automated lifecycle job that runs daily. Deletions are recorded to an immutable audit index and we can provide a filtered slice for your tenant.

5) Exceptions: we do have a documented exceptions process (runbook) for legal/forensics holds. Approvals are captured in the exceptions runbook and linked to change tickets. For customer-approved exceptions (temporary preserves), we can provide the approval ticket id, the approver name, and any compensating controls such as read-only snapshot retention under an encrypted escrow bucket.

Next steps: would you like the artifacts as a ZIP drop or secure Drive folder? I can deliver the initial set by end of day 2027-06-11 if that timeline works. Also proposing a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the auditor through the artifacts — I'm available 10:00–12:00 PT.

Attachments:
- retention-policy-2027.pdf (policy excerpt, policy owner: Neha Kapoor)
- sample-deletion-log-20270610.csv (redacted sample)

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Lead, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped deletion evidence for upcoming audit

Ava / Jonas — quick internal notes to align the evidence package before we send to Medigen: 

- Marco asked explicitly for tenant-scoped proof. We must ensure any samples only contain the Medigen tenant prefix (tenant: medigen-123).
- For the auditor, include:
  * policy PDF (signed/dated)
  * lifecycle rule JSON (s3-lifecycle-medigen.json)
  * deletion CSV (redacted) with the object key hash and deletion timestamp
  * KMS key usage logs showing the delete operation if available (we can provide a filtered KMS event set)
- If Medigen requests evidence of exceptions: reference the exceptions runbook and include the ticket id for the Velatech exception as an example (ticket: DEF-2027-0893) — but redact any unrelated customer identifiers.
- We should attach the internal runbook excerpt (runbook-retention-exceptions.md) and include a short narrative about compensating controls (read-only escrow, HSM-backed key rotation, restricted access group).

I'll prepare the lifecycle JSON and KMS slices; Jonas, can you export the immutable audit index (filter on tenant prefix) and produce a short verification checklist that the auditor can run locally?

Neha
Director, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Marco Salazar <marco.salazar@medigen.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped deletion evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Marco — thanks for the patience. Delivering the package we discussed (zipped and shared via secure Drive link):

- retention-policy-2027.pdf (policy excerpt, signed by Neha Kapoor)
- sample-deletion-log-20270610.csv (redacted: tenant medigen-123 only)
- runbook-retention-exceptions.md (internal excerpt; redacted)
- s3-lifecycle-medigen.json (lifecycle rule applied to medigen-123 prefix)
- kms-event-slice-20270610.csv (filtered KMS key usages related to deletion events)

Secure Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_medigen-evidence

Per our internal compliance guidance, the sample deletion CSV includes hashed object ids (sha256 trunc) and timestamps — no payloads or customer PII. The lifecycle JSON demonstrates the 30-day expiration rule applied to the medigen-123 prefix. The runbook excerpt documents the approval path for temporary holds; if you need the actual ticket metadata for a previously-approved exception we can provide the ticket id and approver under an NDA/limited-scope share.

Please confirm receipt and whether you'd like a 30-min walkthrough with one of our engineers and me; available windows: Monday 06/14 between 10:00–11:30 PT or 14:00–15:00 PT.

Best,
Ava Chen
Lead, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
